title: Using msigdf with enrichment tools
text: msigdf ships gene sets . deliberately depend enrichment package, fgsea clusterProfiler installed alongside . chunks reshape msigdf data evaluated , output see real. chunks call enrichment package marked eval=FALSE shown recipes copy — install relevant Bioconductor package first:
code: # install.packages("BiocManager") BiocManager::install(c("fgsea", "clusterProfiler"))

what: A named list of gene sets
title: Using msigdf with enrichment tools
text: fgsea::fgsea() several tools expect gene sets named list: one element per gene set, holding character vector gene identifiers. split() produces exactly . Using human hallmark collection (category_code == "h"): Feed straight fgsea, together named vector ranking statistics: collection works way. restrict one sub-collection, filter category_subcode well:
code: hallmark <- msigdf.human %>%   filter(category_code == "h")  pathways <- split(hallmark$symbol, hallmark$geneset)  length(pathways) ## [1] 50 lengths(pathways) %>% head() ##        HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION  ##                          200                          200  ##   HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE        HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS  ##                          101                           36  ##     HALLMARK_APICAL_JUNCTION      HALLMARK_APICAL_SURFACE  ##                          200                           44 pathways[["HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING"]] %>% head(10) ##  [1] "APH1A"  "ARRB1"  "CCND1"  "CUL1"   "DLL1"   "DTX1"   "DTX2"   "DTX4"   ##  [9] "FBXW11" "FZD1" library(fgsea)  # `stats` is a named numeric vector: names are gene symbols, values are the # ranking metric (log fold change, signed -log10 p-value, ...). res <- fgsea(pathways = pathways, stats = stats)  res %>%   as_tibble() %>%   arrange(padj) %>%   select(pathway, pval, padj, NES, size) reactome <- msigdf.human %>%   filter(category_code == "c2", category_subcode == "cp.reactome")  reactome_pathways <- split(reactome$symbol, reactome$geneset) length(reactome_pathways) ## [1] 1839

title: Using msigdf with enrichment tools
text: clusterProfiler::enricher() GSEA() take two-column data frame: gene set name first, gene identifier second. msigdf layout minus collection columns. :
code: term2gene <- msigdf.human %>%   filter(category_code == "h") %>%   select(term = geneset, gene = symbol)  term2gene ## # A tibble: 7,322 × 2 ##    term                  gene  ##    <chr>                 <chr> ##  1 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ABCA1 ##  2 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ABCB8 ##  3 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACAA2 ##  4 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACADL ##  5 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACADM ##  6 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACADS ##  7 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACLY  ##  8 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACO2  ##  9 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ACOX1 ## 10 HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS ADCY6 ## # ℹ 7,312 more rows library(clusterProfiler)  # Over-representation on a character vector of gene symbols. ora <- enricher(gene = my_genes, TERM2GENE = term2gene)  # Or GSEA on a sorted, named numeric vector. gsea <- GSEA(geneList = sorted_stats, TERM2GENE = term2gene)

title: Using msigdf with enrichment tools
text: mouse tibble shape. Note collection codes differ: hallmark mh rather h, numbered collections run m1-m8. Mouse gene sets carry mouse symbols, ortholog mapping needed data already mouse.
code: msigdf.mouse %>%   distinct(category_code) %>%   arrange(category_code) ## # A tibble: 7 × 1 ##   category_code ##   <chr>         ## 1 m1            ## 2 m2            ## 3 m3            ## 4 m5            ## 5 m7            ## 6 m8            ## 7 mh mouse_hallmark <- msigdf.mouse %>%   filter(category_code == "mh")  mouse_pathways <- split(mouse_hallmark$symbol, mouse_hallmark$geneset)  length(mouse_pathways) ## [1] 50 mouse_pathways[["HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING"]] %>% head(10) ##  [1] "Aph1a"  "Arrb1"  "Ccnd1"  "Cul1"   "Dll1"   "Dtx1"   "Dtx2"   "Dtx4"   ##  [9] "Fbxw11" "Fzd1"

title: Using msigdf with enrichment tools
text: msigdf.urls msigdf.mouse.urls map every gene set name page MSigDB website. Join enrichment output get clickable links report. join applied fgsea result:
code: top_sets <- msigdf.human %>%   filter(category_code == "h") %>%   count(geneset, name = "n_genes") %>%   arrange(n_genes) %>%   head(5)  top_sets %>%   inner_join(msigdf.urls, by = "geneset") %>%   select(geneset, n_genes, url) ## # A tibble: 5 × 3 ##   geneset                             n_genes url                                ##   <chr>                                 <int> <chr>                              ## 1 HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING                 32 http://software.broadinstitute.or… ## 2 HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS                    36 http://software.broadinstitute.or… ## 3 HALLMARK_HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING              36 http://software.broadinstitute.or… ## 4 HALLMARK_PANCREAS_BETA_CELLS             40 http://software.broadinstitute.or… ## 5 HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING      42 http://software.broadinstitute.or… res %>%   as_tibble() %>%   arrange(padj) %>%   head(20) %>%   inner_join(msigdf.urls, by = c("pathway" = "geneset")) %>%   select(pathway, padj, NES, url)

See script data-raw/ see data frames (tibbles) created.

title: MSigDF: Molecular Signature Database (MSigDB) in a Data Frame
text: four data frames (tibbles) package. msigdf.human data frame columns MSigDB collection divided sub-collection (like cc, bp mf C5). format data tidy, row single gene set collection, sub-collection gene symbol. msigdf.mouse data frame structure mouse collections. msigdf.urls msigdf.mouse.urls data frames link name gene set page MSigDB website. New C5 ontology information added category subcode easy filtering consistency. HPO: Human Phenotype Ontology MF: GO Molecular Function ontology BP: GO Biological Process ontology CC: GO Cellular Component ontology data sets package several million rows. package imports tibble package ’re displayed nicely. Take look: Just get entries KEGG non-homologous end joining pathway: software, e.g., fGSEA might require gene sets named list genes identifiers, name element list name pathway. data originally structured, can return plyr::dlply(). , let’s use hallmark sets, dlply data named list format, get just first pathways, , just display first gene symbols.
